examples.question_text:
Evaluate when $x=-8$. Show the substitution step.
(a) $x+5$
(b) $3x$
(c) $-2x$
examples.solution_text:
(a)
$\begin{align*}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}x+5\\&=(-8)+5\\&=-3\end{align*}$
(b)
$\begin{align*}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}3x\\&=3(-8)\\&=-24\end{align*}$
Unlike signs give a negative product.
(c)
$\begin{align*}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}-2x\\&=-2(-8)\\&=16\end{align*}$
Like signs give a positive product. Keep the negative value in brackets each time it replaces $x$.

examples.question_text:
Evaluate $9-4b$ when $b=-3$.
A student writes $9-4(3)=-3$. Explain the error.
examples.solution_text:
The student used $3$ instead of the given value $-3$.
$\begin{align*}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}9-4b\\&=9-4(-3)\\&=9-(-12)\\&=9+12\\&=21\end{align*}$
Substitute the whole negative value in brackets. Subtracting the negative product becomes adding.

examples.question_text:
Evaluate when $p=-2$. Explain why the answers differ.
(a) $3p^{2}$
(b) $(3p)^{2}$
examples.solution_text:
(a) The square applies only to $p$.
$\begin{align*}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}3p^2\\&=3(-2)^2\\&=3(4)\\&=12\end{align*}$
(b) The square applies to the whole bracket $3p$.
$\begin{align*}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}(3p)^2\\&=(3(-2))^2\\&=(-6)^2\\&=36\end{align*}$
In (a), square the substituted value before multiplying by $3$. In (b), work out the whole bracket before squaring.

(a) Replace each pronumeral with its own negative value.
$\begin{align*}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}2a-5b\\&=2(-4)-5(-3)\\&=-8-(-15)\\&=-8+15\\&=7\end{align*}$
(b) Evaluate the powers first.
$\begin{align*}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}a^3+b^2\\&=(-4)^3+(-3)^2\\&=-64+9\\&=-55\end{align*}$
Three negative factors give a negative cube. Two negative factors give a positive square.

examples.question_text: Evaluate $\frac{3x+5}{4}$ when $x=-4$. Give an exact fraction.
examples.solution_text:
Substitute the negative value in brackets. Work out the whole numerator before dividing.
$\begin{align*}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{3x+5}{4}\\&=\frac{3(-4)+5}{4}\\&=\frac{-12+5}{4}\\&=\frac{-7}{4}\\&=-\frac{7}{4}\end{align*}$

examples.question_text:
Evaluate when $x=-5$.
(a) $x^{2}$
(b) $-x^{2}$
Explain what the minus sign in (b) applies to.
examples.solution_text:
(a)
$\begin{align*}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}x^2\\&=(-5)^2\\&=(-5)(-5)\\&=25\end{align*}$
(b)
$\begin{align*}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}-x^2\\&=-\left((-5)^2\right)\\&=-25\end{align*}$
The substituted value is bracketed in both expressions. In (b), the extra minus sign is outside the power, so take the negative of the completed square.

(a) Substitute each value in its own place, then evaluate the products.
$\begin{align*}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}3ab+ac\\&=3(-3)(4)+(-3)(-2)\\&=-36+6\\&=-30\end{align*}$
(b) Evaluate the square and the product before subtracting.
$\begin{align*}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}a^2-2ac\\&=(-3)^2-2(-3)(-2)\\&=9-12\\&=-3\end{align*}$

(a) Substitute the same bracketed value for every $x$.
$\begin{align*}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}x^2-2x+1\\&=(-2)^2-2(-2)+1\\&=4-(-4)+1\\&=4+4+1\\&=9\end{align*}$
(b) Evaluate the square before subtracting.
$\begin{align*}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}x-x^2\\&=(-2)-(-2)^2\\&=-2-4\\&=-6\end{align*}$

examples.derivation: For x=-8: (-8)+5=-3; 3(-8)=-24; -2(-8)=16. Bracketed substitution and product signs match the supplied algebra exercises.
4(-3)=-12, so 9-4(-3)=9-(-12)=21. The student substituted positive 3 instead of negative 3, matching the source's error-analysis method.
3(-2)^2=3(4)=12; (3(-2))^2=(-6)^2=36. The power-scope comparison matches the supplied Indices exercises and remains a useful supplementary example.
2(-4)-5(-3)=-8-(-15)=7. (-4)^3+(-3)^2=-64+9=-55. Both follow the source's substitution and operation order.
3(-4)+5=-12+5=-7, giving -7/4 exactly. Evaluating the whole numerator before division matches Guided Practice e.
(-5)^2=25; -((-5)^2)=-25. The additional minus applies after squaring, matching the supplied Indices card comparison.
3(-3)(4)+(-3)(-2)=-36+6=-30. (-3)^2-2(-3)(-2)=9-12=-3. Products, repeated substitution and squares are supported by the supplied algebra exercises.
(-2)^2-2(-2)+1=4-(-4)+1=9. (-2)-(-2)^2=-2-4=-6. Both use bracketed repeated substitution and the supplied order-of-operations method.
